captions.detailed: A classic woodworking front vise consisting of a wide, dark brown wooden fixed jaw plate meant for bench mounting, a matching lighter brown wooden moving jaw, and two parallel steel guide rods. A central threaded metal lead screw passes through the jaws, connected to a black metal hub with a silver sliding handle bar capped with wooden end knobs. The moving jaw translates linearly along the guide rods, while the lead-screw handle rotates continuously to drive the clamping mechanism.
captions.instruction: Generate a parametric 3D model of a woodworking front vise. The assembly should include a fixed rear wooden jaw, a moving front wooden jaw that translates along horizontal steel guide rods, and a threaded central lead screw with a rotating handle hub and sliding metal bar with wooden end caps.
captions.factory: Construct a fixed jaw using a rounded Box primitive. Create the moving jaw as a separate part using a similarly styled Box. Add guide rods and a central lead screw using Cylinder primitives, applying a helical sweep or concentric cylinders for the screw threads. Model the handle assembly with a central cylinder hub, a thin perpendicular cylinder for the sliding bar, and small capped cylinders at the ends. Set up a prismatic joint for the moving jaw along the horizontal guide axes, and a continuous rotational joint for the lead screw and handle.
